III.|OF THE APOSTLES.|297}}</noinclude>temple. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=3}}† He, vvhen he had seen Peter and Iohn about to enter into the temple, asked to receiue an almes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}}† But Peter vvith Iohn looking vpon him, said, Looke vpon vs. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}}† But he looked earnestly vpon them, hoping that he should receiue some thing of them. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}}† But Peter said, Siluer and gold I haue not, but {{sup|‖}} that vvhich I haue, the same I giue to thee: In the name of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} of Nazareth arise, and vvalke. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}}† And taking his right hand, he lifted him vp, and forthvvith his feete and soles vvere made strong. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}}† And springing he stoode, and vvalked: and vvent in vvith them into the temple vvalking, and leaping, and praising God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}}† And al the people savv him vvalking and praising God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}}† And they knevv him, that, it vvas he vvhich sate for almes at the Specious gate of the temple: and they vvere excedingly astonied and agast at that that had chaunced to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}}† And as he held Peter and Iohn, al the people ranne to them vnto the porche vvhich is called Salomons, vvondering.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpõ wenesday in Easter weeke.}}But Peter seing them, made ansvver to the people, Ye men of Israël, vvhy maruel you at this, or vvhy looke you vpon vs, as though {{sup|‖}} by our povver or holines vve haue made this man to vvalke? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}}† The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob, the God of our fathers hath glorified his sonne {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhom you in deede deliuered and denied before the face of Pilate, he iudging him to be released. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}}† But you denied the holy and the iust one, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 23, 18.''}}* and asked a man killer to be giuen vnto you. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}}† but the authour of life you killed, vvhom God hath raised from the dead, of vvhich vve are vvitnesses. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}}† And in the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This faith was not the faith of the lame man (for he looked onely for almes) nor a special faith of the Apostles owne saluatiõ: but the whole beleefe of Christian Religion.}}∷ faith of his name, this man vvhom you see and knovv, his name hath strengthened: & the faith vvhich is by him, hath giuen this perfect health in the sight of al you.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}}† And novv (brethren) I knovv that you did it through ignorance, as also your princes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}}† But God vvho foreshevved by the mouth of al the prophets, that his {{sc|Christ}} should suffer, hath so fulfilled it. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}}† Be Penitent therfore & conuert, that your sinnes may be put out.⊣ {{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}}† that, vvhen the times shal come of refreshing by the sight of our Lord, and he shal send him that hath been preached vnto you {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι''}}∷ vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Some Heretikes fouly corrupt this place, thus, ''Who must be conteined in heauen'', of purpose (as they protest) to hold Christ in heauẽ, from the B. Sacramẽt. ''Beza''. As though his presẽce there, drew him out of heauen. Neither cã they pretend the Greeke, vvhich is vvord for word as in the vulgar latin, and as we translate.}}∷ heauen truely must receiue vntil the times of the restitution of al things, vvhich God spake by the mouth of his holy prophets from the beginning of the world.<noinclude>{{rh||Pp|Moyses}}</noinclude>
